entries.proposition: The commentary is on a single gastrointestinal stromal tumour paper (ref 8, toosendanin and NCOA4 ferritinophagy); it makes no measurement.
entries.snippet: A recently reported study by Feng et al. in the Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology (8) describes the ability of toosendanin

entries.proposition: The commentator calls the single-cell-line design a significant weakness of the commented study.
entries.snippet: The use of a single cell line (GIST-T1 cells) is a significant weakness in this investigation.

entries.proposition: The only WWOX statement: citing ref 14, toosendanin activates WWOX, raising p53 and suppressing NRF2 activity, lowering GPX4 and SLC7A11 and, as written here, increasing the iron exporter SLC40A1.
entries.snippet: activation of WWOX leading to increased transcriptional activity of p53 and suppressed transcriptional activity of NRF2, thus leading to decreased expression of GPX4 and SLC7A11 and increased expression of the iron exporter SLC40A1 (14)

entries.proposition: Ref 14 as listed (the WWOX hepatocellular carcinoma paper whose abstract reports DECREASED SLC40A1, so the commentary's 'increased' disagrees with the abstract of its own source).
entries.snippet: WWOX-mediated p53/SAT1 and NRF2/FPN1 axis contribute to toosendanin-induced ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma.

entries.proposition: The STAT3 hypothesis is stated as a posited explanation, and the paper's own title asks it as a question.
entries.snippet: we posit that STAT3 as the upstream pharmacological target for toosendanin may convincingly explain the changes

entries.proposition: The STAT3 SH2 binding statement carries citation (17), which in the reference list is a toosendanin paper on Nrf2 O-GlcNAcylation, not the osteosarcoma STAT3 paper listed as ref 18.
entries.snippet: Toosendanin directly binds to the SH2 domain of STAT3 with a KD value of ~0.24 µM (17).
Toosendanin sensitizes hepatocyte ferroptosis via dual inhibition of Nrf2 O-GlcNAcylation and USP7-driven deubiquitination.
